summary.intent: The user noticed that recent todos were being filed as GitHub issues instead of using the established `/gsd:capture --todo` file workflow, and wanted the two misfiled items (#547 GC, #549 IPNS verify-caching) migrated to the correct location and the issues closed.
summary.outcome: Root cause identified as assistant drift (not a config change). Two todo files were created in `.planning/todos/pending/` on a docs branch matching existing frontmatter conventions, staged and committed. Issues #547 and #549 are pending closure.

repo: Todos live in `.planning/todos/pending/` and `.planning/todos/completed/` as markdown files with structured frontmatter (area, severity, etc.); they are git-tracked and numbered by reference.
GSD capture workflow uses `/gsd:capture --todo` skill — never `gh issue create` — for personal task tracking.
`.planning/config.json` has no issue-routing for capture; GitHub issues are not the intended destination for todos in this repo.
workflow: When rich investigation writeups (Context / Scope / Acceptance) emerge from deep technical sessions, they can superficially feel like GitHub issues but should still go through the file-todo workflow.
History in `history.jsonl` is the authoritative record for what the user typed vs. what the assistant did — useful for diagnosing behavioral drift.
When migrating misfiled issues to file-todos, open a docs branch, write the files, commit/push/PR, then close the source issues with a pointer.

friction: The `gsd:capture` skill body was not findable via content search — required indirect discovery through plugin manifests and marketplace paths.
Two todos existed only as GitHub issues with no corresponding file-todo, requiring manual migration work.
open_items: Push the docs branch and open the PR for the two migrated todo files.
Close GitHub issues #547 (periodic GC) and #549 (IPNS verify-caching) with a pointer to the new file-todos once the branch is merged.
